mainTopic: Liability for slaughtering and offering up outside: partners, the arguments of רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי about איש איש and ההוא, offering up in parts, and whether a real מזבח is needed.
overview: The amud opens by explaining why the word ההוא ("that man") exempts two partners who slaughter outside, but not two partners who offer up outside. The slaughtering פסוק writes ההוא twice, and the offering-up פסוק writes it only once. The word לה׳ is explained as excluding the שעיר המשתלח. Next, a ברייתא brings the argument between רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי. רבי שמעון learns from איש איש that partners who offer up together are liable. רבי יוסי learns from ההוא that they are exempt, and he treats איש איש as ordinary speech. The גמרא then asks what the משנה's argument about offering up several times is really about. ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן, two versions of עולא and אבוה דשמואל each give an answer, built on whole limbs versus incomplete parts and parts meant for inside versus outside. The amud then gives each side's proof on whether a real מזבח is needed: נח's altar for רבי יוסי, and מנוח's rock and a ברייתא for רבי שמעון. It ends with a ruling that the altar's corner, ramp, base and square shape are required on a public במה but not on a private one.

steps.title: "That man" in offering up excludes people who did not act on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The word ההוא in the פסוק about offering up outside is needed to exclude a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה. So it cannot also teach that two people together are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed to exclude one who acted unknowingly, one who was forced, and one who was mistaken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question. The word ההוא in the offering-up פסוק is already being used for something else, so it does not exempt two people who offer up together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was why ההוא doesn't exempt two people in offering up, the way it does in slaughtering. The answer: in offering up, ההוא teaches that only a person acting on purpose gets כרת. A שוגג, an אנוס or a מוטעה does not. Since the word is used up for that lesson, there is nothing left to exempt partners.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the word is needed for a different lesson)
One who was mistaken or misled

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a conversation. The word ההוא is the one in the פסוק about offering up outside (ויקרא 17:9), not the one about slaughtering.

phrases.english: It is needed to exclude
phrases.notes: "It" is the word ההוא ("that man") in the פסוק about offering up outside, ויקרא 17:9.

phrases.english: one who acted unknowingly, one who was forced, and one who was mistaken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked just before this section: why ההוא doesn't exempt partners in offering up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is needed for a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ההוא appears in the offering-up פסוק, two people offering up together should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: In offering up, ההוא only excludes a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה, so partners remain liable.

steps.title: Slaughtering should need that same exclusion
steps.stepSummary: If ההוא is needed to exclude a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה, the slaughtering פסוק should need it for that too. Then it could not teach that partners are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, here too, it is needed to exclude one who was forced, one who acted unknowingly, and one who was mistaken!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The same reasoning seems to apply to the slaughtering פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering outside also needs a source to exclude a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה from כרת. If ההוא in the slaughtering פסוק is used for that, it can no longer teach that two people slaughtering together are exempt. The new answer seems to knock out the old teaching.

phrases.english: If so, here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case of slaughtering outside.

phrases.english: it is needed to exclude one who was forced, one who acted unknowingly, and one who was mistaken!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 1 against the earlier teaching about slaughtering.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that ההוא in the slaughtering פסוק exempts partners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughtering also needs to exclude a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה. So ההוא should be used up there too, leaving no source to exempt partners.

steps.title: The slaughtering verse says "that man" twice
steps.stepSummary: The slaughtering פסוק writes ההוא twice. One teaches that only a person acting on purpose is liable, and the other teaches that only one person acting alone is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two instances of "that" man are written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The slaughtering פסוק has two extra words, so it can teach two lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 17:4 says both "דם יחשב לאיש ההוא" and "ונכרת האיש ההוא". With two appearances of ההוא, one excludes a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה, and the other exempts partners. The offering-up פסוק has only one ההוא, so it teaches only the first lesson.
steps.whatToRemember: Slaughtering outside: two people together are exempt, because ההוא is written twice. Offering up outside: two people together are liable, because ההוא is written only once and is needed to exclude a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה.

phrases.english: Two instances of "that" man are written.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughtering has only one ההוא, and it is used up excluding a שוגג.
steps.terutzMaskana: Slaughtering has two, so one excludes a שוגג and the other exempts partners.

steps.title: Then what does "to the Lord" teach?
steps.stepSummary: The liability for slaughtering for an ordinary purpose comes from איש איש. So the גמרא asks why the slaughtering פסוק needs the word לה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need "to the Lord"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word לה׳ in the slaughtering פסוק is teaching. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא based the liability for slaughtering outside for an ordinary purpose on the words איש איש. That leaves the word לה׳ ("להקריב קרבן לה׳") with no job, so the גמרא asks what it is for.

phrases.english: But why do I need "to the Lord"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that ההוא and איש איש are explained, the גמרא asks about another word in the same פסוק.

steps.title: "To the Lord" excludes the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: The word לה׳ excludes the שעיר המשתלח. Someone who slaughters it outside is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude the scapegoat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that לה׳ teaches that slaughtering the שעיר המשתלח outside does not make a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעיר המשתלח of יום כיפור is sent away to עזאזל. It is not offered on the מזבח "to the Lord." So the word לה׳ limits the liability to animals that are meant for ה׳'s מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The scapegoat sent away on יום כיפור

phrases.english: To exclude the scapegoat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לה׳ excludes the שעיר המשתלח from liability for slaughtering outside.

steps.title: New topic: the greater stringency of offering up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Two people who offer up a limb together outside are liable, unlike two who slaughter together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The greater stringency with regard to offering up, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a discussion of that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that two people slaughtering outside together are exempt, but two people offering up a limb together are liable. Steps 1–3 already explained the source for this difference. Now the גמרא opens a discussion of this line itself.

phrases.english: The greater stringency with regard to offering up, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points to the rest of the משנה: two who offer up a limb together outside are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering up outside is more stringent: partners who offer up together are liable, while partners who slaughter together are exempt.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: Two who offer up a limb together are liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that איש איש makes two people who offer up a limb together liable. A פסוק is needed because a קל וחומר from slaughtering would have exempted them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Why does the פסוק say "איש איש"? To teach that two people who held a limb and offered it up are liable. This needs a פסוק, because you might have thought there is a logical proof to exempt them. Slaughtering for an ordinary purpose is liable, yet two who held a knife and slaughtered together are exempt. Offering up for an ordinary purpose is exempt to begin with. So surely two who offer up together should also be exempt! That is why the פסוק says "איש איש". This is the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain the line of the משנה quoted in step 6. רבי שמעון learns from איש איש that two people who offer up together are liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering is the stricter case, because it is liable even for an ordinary purpose, and yet partners are exempt there. So you would think partners are surely exempt for offering up, which is the more lenient case. The extra word איש tells us not to follow that קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: "Any man" (literally "a man, a man"), a doubled word in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר here is the thought the פסוק rejects. It is not the final ruling. רבי שמעון's final ruling is that partners who offer up together ARE liable.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Any man" (ish ish): what does the verse teach?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8, the פסוק about offering up a sacrifice outside.

phrases.english: That two who held a limb and offered it up are liable.
For one might say: is it not logical?
If one who slaughters for an ordinary purpose, who is liable,
still, two who held a knife and slaughtered are exempt;
then with one who offers up for an ordinary purpose, who is exempt,
is it not logical that two who held it together are exempt?
So the verse says "ish ish".
These are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ – מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the line of the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, two who offer up a limb together outside are liable, learned from איש איש.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: ההוא means one person, not two
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns from the single word ההוא that only one person acting alone is liable for offering up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: "That" (ההוא) man means one person, and not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's opposite view. He holds that two who offer up together are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי reads the singular word ההוא in the פסוק about offering up as limiting liability to one person alone. This goes against רבי שמעון's ruling that partners are liable.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
"That" man: one and not two.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two who offer up together outside are exempt, because ההוא means one person alone.

steps.title: What does רבי יוסי do with איש איש?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how רבי יוסי explains the doubled word איש איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say "איש איש"?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question about רבי יוסי's view and sets up the answer in the next step. If he does not learn liability for partners from איש איש, why is the word doubled?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an extra word in the תורה teaches something. רבי יוסי must explain what the extra איש is for.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״?
phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach with "ish ish"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי יוסי's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the doubled word איש איש teaches according to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The תורה speaks like people speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the doubled איש איש is just normal speech and teaches nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה spoke the way people normally speak.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question in step 9. To רבי יוסי, איש איש is just a normal way of saying "any man".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם, a doubled word can be ordinary style rather than a hint. So nothing can be learned from איש איש.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה spoke in the language of people, so extra wording is just style

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule comes back in step 13, where it causes a new problem for רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: איש איש is ordinary human speech and teaches nothing.

steps.title: רבי שמעון uses ההוא for other exclusions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון needs ההוא to exclude a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה, so it cannot teach about partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? He needs this word ההוא to exclude someone who acted by mistake, someone who was forced, and someone who was misled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון does not learn from ההוא that partners are exempt. He uses the word for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is left unsaid: what does רבי שמעון do with ההוא? The answer is that ההוא limits liability to someone acting on purpose. So the word is already used up and cannot also exempt partners.

keyTerms.meaning: This (one), pointing to the word ההוא in the פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon?
He needs this word "that"
to exclude one who acted unwittingly, one forced, or one mistaken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not accept רבי יוסי's reading of ההוא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ההוא is used to exclude a שוגג, an אנוס and a מוטעה.

steps.title: הוא versus ההוא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns the exclusion of a שוגג from the extra ה in ההוא. רבי שמעון does not learn anything from that extra ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי learns that from the change from הוא to ההוא. And רבי שמעון does not learn anything from the change from הוא to ההוא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוסי can get both teachings out of one word. It also explains why רבי שמעון cannot do the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said הוא and instead said ההוא. רבי יוסי reads the extra ה as a second teaching, so the word covers both the שוגג exclusion and the partners rule. רבי שמעון does not read anything into that extra letter, so for him the word gives only one teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not learn anything from it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei learns it from "hu" becoming "hahu".
phrases.notes: The פסוק could have just said הוא; the extra ה gives רבי יוסי a second teaching.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon does not learn anything from "hu" becoming "hahu".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוסי deals with the need from step 11, and why רבי שמעון cannot.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי learns the שוגג exclusion from the extra ה. רבי שמעון does not learn anything from that extra ה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: איש איש makes partners liable, and ההוא excludes a שוגג. רבי יוסי: ההוא makes partners exempt, the extra ה excludes a שוגג, and איש איש is just ordinary speech.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי learn liability for slaughtering for an ordinary purpose?
steps.stepSummary: If איש איש is just ordinary speech for רבי יוסי, the same should be true in the slaughtering פסוק. Then where does he learn that slaughtering for an ordinary purpose is liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי: since this איש איש is just how people speak, that איש איש in the slaughtering פסוק should also be just how people speak. If so, where does he learn that someone who slaughters for an ordinary purpose is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי. Step 4 said the liability for slaughtering for an ordinary purpose comes from איש איש, and now that source seems gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי treats איש איש as ordinary speech in the offering-up פסוק, he should do the same in the slaughtering פסוק. But then he has lost his source for the rule that slaughtering for an ordinary purpose is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei:
since this "ish ish"
is the Torah speaking in the language of people,
that "ish ish" also
phrases.notes: The איש איש in the slaughtering פסוק, ויקרא 17:3.

phrases.english: is the Torah speaking in the language of people.
But then, one who slaughters for an ordinary purpose:
from where does he know that he is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי – מִדְּהַאי ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוסי's rule from step 10 to the slaughtering פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's source for liability when slaughtering for an ordinary purpose.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If איש איש teaches nothing in one פסוק, it should teach nothing in the other, so that rule has no source.

steps.title: Learned from דם יחשב לאיש ההוא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns the liability for slaughtering for an ordinary purpose from the words לאיש ההוא, which include slaughtering for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "Blood shall be counted to that man; he has shed blood". This includes even someone who slaughters for a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 13 by giving רבי יוסי a different פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לאיש can be read as "for a man". So the פסוק includes slaughtering for the sake of a person, meaning an ordinary purpose. This way רבי יוסי does not need איש איש for this rule.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's source for liability when slaughtering for an ordinary purpose is "דם יחשב לאיש ההוא", not איש איש.

phrases.english: He learns it

phrases.aramaic: מִ״דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב לָאִישׁ הַהוּא דָּם שָׁפָךְ״ –
phrases.english: from "Blood shall be counted to that man; he has shed blood":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4.

phrases.english: even one who slaughters for a man.
phrases.notes: He reads לאיש as "for a man", meaning slaughtering for an ordinary person's use, not for ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב לָאִישׁ הַהוּא דָּם שָׁפָךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seemed to have no source for this rule once איש איש was treated as ordinary speech.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns it from the words לאיש ההוא in ויקרא 17:4.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about someone who offered up parts of an offering outside at separate times.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he offered up part of an offering outside, then went back and offered up more, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the explanations that come right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון says each separate act of offering up outside needs its own חטאת. רבי יוסי says he brings only one חטאת. The next steps ask what case this argument is really about.

keyTerms.meaning: He offered up (burned on a מזבח)

phrases.english: He offered up, and went back and offered up, etc.
phrases.notes: Each time he forgot it was forbidden, so each time counts as a separate mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of steps 10-14 (איש איש and slaughtering) and moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה: רבי שמעון makes him liable for each act of offering up, and רבי יוסי makes him liable only once.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: they argue about several whole limbs
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the argument is about four or five limbs offered up at separate times. Everyone agrees that one limb in pieces gets only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the argument is about four or five limbs. רבי יוסי holds that the פסוק 'to sacrifice it' (you are liable for something whole, not something missing) means the whole animal. רבי שמעון holds it means each limb. But for one limb, everyone agrees he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains what case the משנה is arguing about. He says it is about several whole limbs, offered up one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לעשות אתו' teaches that you are liable only for offering up something whole. רבי יוסי says 'whole' means the whole animal, so all the limbs together make one חטאת. רבי שמעון says each limb is its own 'whole', so each limb gets its own חטאת. Pieces of one limb count as one for everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' here is רבי יוסי (whole animal) and the second 'מר' is רבי שמעון (each limb). The order of the two מר's changes in the next steps, so check who is who each time.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The dispute is about four or five limbs;
For one master holds: when it is written 'to sacrifice it' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:9. This 'מר' is רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: that for a whole item he is liable
and he is not liable for an incomplete item,
it is written about the whole animal;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אַכֹּל אֵבֶר וְאֵבֶר כְּתִיב.
phrases.english: And the other master holds: it is written about each and every limb.
But one limb –

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: everyone agrees he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּאַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which case the משנה quoted in step 15 is arguing about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is about several limbs: for רבי יוסי the whole animal is one unit, for רבי שמעון each limb is a unit. One limb in pieces gets only one חטאת according to everyone.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: they argue about one limb from an offering meant for inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the argument is about one limb offered up in pieces outside. Everyone agrees that several limbs get a חטאת each.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the argument is about one limb. One master holds that parts meant to be burned inside, which became incomplete and were offered up outside, make him liable. The other master holds he is exempt. But for four or five limbs, everyone agrees he is liable for each limb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different explanation of the משנה. He says the argument is about pieces of one limb, not about several limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limb came from an offering that was supposed to be burned on the מזבח inside, and it lost a part. רבי שמעון says offering up such an incomplete piece outside still makes him liable, so each piece gets a חטאת. רבי יוסי says an incomplete piece makes him exempt. For several whole limbs, both agree each limb is its own חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Parts meant to be burned inside (on the מזבח in the עזרה)
That became incomplete, lost a part

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The dispute is about one limb –
For one master holds: parts to be burned inside that became incomplete
phrases.notes: Here the first 'מר' is רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: and he offered them up outside – he is liable,
phrases.notes: Some versions say the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'offered them up'.

phrases.english: And the other master holds – he is exempt;
But with four or five limbs –

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אֵבֶר וְאֵבֶר.
phrases.english: everyone agrees he is liable for each and every limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּאֵבֶר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש in step 16. What ריש לקיש said everyone agrees on (one limb) is where רבי יוחנן puts the argument, and the reverse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is about an incomplete limb meant to be burned inside: רבי שמעון says liable, רבי יוסי says exempt. Several limbs get a חטאת each according to everyone.

steps.title: עולא: they argue only about parts already fit only for outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן disagrees with עולא. עולא says everyone agrees about parts meant for inside, and the argument is only about parts that were to be burned outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with עולא, because עולא said: everyone agrees that parts meant to be burned inside, which became incomplete and were offered up outside, make him liable. They argue only about parts burned outside that became incomplete and were offered up outside. One master holds he is exempt, and the other holds he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings עולא, whose view clashes with רבי יוחנן. עולא moves the argument to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the incomplete part meant for inside is the case they argue about. עולא says everyone agrees he is liable there. The argument is only about an offering slaughtered outside, so its parts were never fit for the inside מזבח: רבי יוסי says exempt and רבי שמעון says liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Parts that would be burned outside (from an offering slaughtered outside)

steps.whatToRemember: Three views of the משנה: ריש לקיש says the argument is about several limbs. רבי יוחנן says it is about one incomplete limb meant for inside. עולא says everyone agrees about the inside case, and they argue only about an incomplete part that was already fit only for outside.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Ulla,
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן's explanation clashes with עולא's.

phrases.english: for Ulla said: Everyone agrees
about parts to be burned inside that became incomplete
and he offered them up outside – that he is liable.
They argued only
about parts to be burned outside that became incomplete
and he offered them up outside –

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר פָּטוּר, וּמַר סָבַר חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: for one master holds he is exempt, and the other master holds he is liable.
phrases.notes: Here the first 'מר' is רבי יוסי (exempt) and the second is רבי שמעון (liable).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּעוּלָּא, דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that רבי יוחנן's view in step 17 conflicts with עולא, and quotes עולא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that an incomplete part meant for inside, offered up outside, makes him liable. The argument is only about an incomplete part meant for outside: רבי יוסי says exempt, רבי שמעון says liable.

steps.title: A second version of עולא's statement
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, עולא says everyone agrees one is exempt for offering up outside parts that were meant to be burned outside. The argument between רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון is only about parts meant for inside that became incomplete.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say עולא said it this way: Everyone agrees that if parts meant to be burned outside became incomplete and someone offered them up outside, he is exempt. They argue only about parts meant to be burned inside that became incomplete and were offered up outside. One master holds he is exempt, and the other holds he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what עולא said. In this report the two cases are switched compared to the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 18), everyone agreed about the inside parts, and the argument was about the outside parts. Here it is the other way around: the outside parts get an exemption according to everyone, and the argument is about the inside parts. In this version, רבי יוסי says exempt and רבי שמעון says liable, so עולא no longer disagrees with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Parts that are to be burned outside (they can never go on the inside מזבח)
One master holds ... and the other master holds

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. Version one: the argument is about the outside parts. Version two (here): the argument is about the inside parts.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Ulla said:
Everyone agrees regarding parts that are to be burned outside
phrases.notes: These are offerings slaughtered outside the Temple. They could never go on the inside מזבח anyway.

phrases.english: that became incomplete and he offered them up outside
phrases.notes: The round-bracket word is in the regular printing, and the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. It means 'offered them up.'

phrases.english: that he is exempt.
They disagree only regarding parts that are to be burned inside
that became incomplete and he offered them up outside,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר פָּטוּר, וּמַר סָבַר חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: as one master holds he is exempt, and the other master holds he is liable.
phrases.notes: The first master is רבי יוסי (exempt), and the second is רבי שמעון (liable).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of עולא's statement from step 18 and reverses which case is agreed upon.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees one is exempt for outside parts that became incomplete. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון argue only about inside parts that became incomplete and were offered up outside.

steps.title: שמואל's father disagrees with the first version of עולא
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל says that returning limbs that jumped off the מזבח is not according to רבי יוסי. This disagrees with the first version of עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The statement of אבוה דשמואל disagrees with the first version of עולא. אבוה דשמואל said: According to whom do we return limbs that jumped off back onto the מזבח? Not according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another אמורא, אבוה דשמואל, holds a view that conflicts with the first version of עולא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבוה דשמואל understands that according to רבי יוסי, incomplete limbs that fell off the מזבח are never put back on it. So someone who offers such limbs outside would be exempt. The first version of עולא said everyone, even רבי יוסי, agrees one is liable for inside parts that became incomplete. That assumes such parts do go back on the מזבח, so the two views clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs that jumped off the fire of the מזבח

phrases.english: And the statement of Shmuel's father disagrees
phrases.notes: The round-bracket word is in the regular printing, and the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. Both mean 'disagree.'

phrases.english: with the first version of Ulla's statement;
phrases.notes: This is the version from step 18, where the argument was about the outside parts.

phrases.english: as Shmuel's father said:
In accordance with whom do we return limbs that jumped off back onto the altar?
In accordance with whom? Not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַלִּישָּׁנָא קַמָּא דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second version of עולא, the גמרא notes that אבוה דשמואל conflicts with the first version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning limbs that jumped off to the מזבח is not according to רבי יוסי. This conflicts with the first version of עולא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's source: נח built an altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that רבי יוסי requires a real מזבח for liability. רב הונא explains his source: נח built a מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: He is not liable until he offers it up on top of a מזבח. רב הונא said: What is רבי יוסי's reason? Because it is written: 'And נח built a מזבח to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the משנה and gives the source for רבי יוסי's view that offering up outside counts only on a real מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח had rocks around him, but he went to the trouble of building a מזבח. This shows that 'offering up' means placing something on a מזבח. So putting an offering on a rock outside the Temple would not make one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: And he is not liable until he offers it up, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה: 'on top of a מזבח.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי?
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?
As it is written: "And Noach built an altar to ה׳."
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of incomplete parts and turns to a new part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי learns from נח building a מזבח that liability for offering up outside requires a real מזבח.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's source: מנוח offered on a rock
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי שמעון learns from מנוח, who offered on a rock, that offering on a rock also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What is רבי שמעון's reason? Because it is written: 'And מנוח took the young goat and the meal offering, and offered it up on the rock to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for the other side, רבי שמעון, who says one is liable even for offering on a rock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls מנוח's act on a rock 'offering up.' So placing an offering on a rock is also considered offering up, and one is liable for doing it outside the Temple. This balances רב הונא's proof for רבי יוסי from נח.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: liability for offering outside only on a real מזבח, learned from נח. רבי שמעון: even on a rock, learned from מנוח.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
As it is written: "And Manoach took the young goat

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת הַמִּנְחָה וַיַּעַל עַל הַצּוּר לַה׳״.
phrases.english: and the meal offering, and offered it up on the rock to ה׳."
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:19

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opposing view, right after רבי יוסי's source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון learns from מנוח offering on a rock that offering up on a rock outside also makes one liable.

steps.title: How does רבי שמעון explain נח's altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: the תורה says נח built a real מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, 'And he built an altar to the Lord'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון and asks how he deals with the פסוק that רבי יוסי uses as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי learned from נח that a real מזבח is needed. If the פסוק clearly says נח built a מזבח, how can רבי שמעון say a plain rock is enough?

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other תנא

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is רבי שמעון. How does he read רבי יוסי's פסוק?

phrases.english: but isn't it written: "And he built an altar to the Lord"!
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:20, about נח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון using רבי יוסי's source from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that offering on a rock counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says נח built a real מזבח, so a real מזבח seems to be needed.

steps.title: נח's altar was just a raised place
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads נח's 'מזבח' as simply a high spot, not a built altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was merely a raised place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי שמעון: the word 'מזבח' in נח's story just means a raised spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נח's מזבח was only a high place, then the פסוק does not prove that a built altar is required. So רבי שמעון's view stands.

phrases.english: That is merely a raised place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נח's מזבח was a real built altar, so one is required.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only a raised place, so nothing is proven.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי explain מנוח's rock?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי: מנוח offered on a rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, 'And מנוח took' and offered on the rock?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to רבי יוסי and asks how he deals with רבי שמעון's proof from מנוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learned from מנוח that a rock works. If מנוח really offered on a rock, how can רבי יוסי say a real מזבח is required?

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: This time 'the other one' is רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: but it is written: "And Manoah took"!
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:19. The פסוק goes on to say he offered it on the rock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror challenge, this time against רבי יוסי, using רבי שמעון's source from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that a real מזבח is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנוח offered on a plain rock, so a rock seems to be valid.

steps.title: מנוח's rock was a one-time ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the case of מנוח was a special ruling for that moment only.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a ruling for that time only.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי: מנוח's offering on a rock was a one-time exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling given only for a special moment cannot teach the normal הלכה. So we cannot learn from מנוח that a rock is generally fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A one-time ruling for special circumstances

steps.whatToRemember: Each side explains away the other's פסוק. רבי שמעון says נח's 'מזבח' was just a raised place. רבי יוסי says מנוח's rock was a הוראת שעה.

phrases.english: It was a ruling for that time only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a special exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מנוח's rock shows that a rock is always valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a one-time ruling, so no general rule can be learned from it.

steps.title: A second source for רבי שמעון from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns that a במה needs no built altar, since the פסוק ties 'מזבח' to the אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say that רבי שמעון's reason comes from a ברייתא. רבי שמעון says: the פסוק says 'the altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.' So a built altar is not needed for a במה. Therefore, one who offered on a rock or a stone is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason for רבי שמעון's view, quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions a מזבח only 'at the entrance of the אהל מועד'. That means a built altar is required only at the main sanctuary, not at a במה. So a rock counts as a proper place of offering, and offering on it outside makes one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead
A private altar, used when this was allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Read alone, the ברייתא seems to talk about a time when במות were allowed, so 'liable' sounds strange. The next steps fix exactly this problem.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
this is the reason of Rabbi Shimon –
as it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
"the altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:6.

phrases.english: but there is no altar required at a private altar;
phrases.notes: He means a built altar is needed only at the אהל מועד, not at a private במה.

phrases.english: therefore, if one offered up

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַסֶּלַע אוֹ עַל הָאֶבֶן – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: on a rock or on a stone – he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second source for רבי שמעון in place of מנוח (step 22).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A built altar is not required at a במה, so offering on a rock outside makes one liable.

steps.title: Shouldn't it say he fulfilled his obligation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says 'liable' and not 'fulfilled his obligation'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have said 'he fulfilled his obligation'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was talking about a במה, which is used when במות are allowed. At such a time, offering on a rock would be a valid offering, so the right word would be 'יצא' (he fulfilled it), not 'חייב' (he is liable).

phrases.english: It should have said "he fulfilled his obligation"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the final word of the ברייתא in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word חייב in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When במות are allowed, a rock offering is valid, so 'liable' does not fit.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a time when במות were forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is explained as speaking about a time when במות were forbidden, so offering on a rock makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: therefore, at a time when במות are forbidden, one who offered on a rock or a stone is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא so that 'liable' makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a rock is a valid place to offer when במות are allowed, it also counts as a real 'offering' when במות are forbidden. So offering on a rock at that time is a forbidden outside offering, and one is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: The time when private altars are forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, a rock is a valid altar for a במה. That is why offering on a rock when במות are forbidden makes one liable.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
therefore, at a time when private altars are forbidden –

phrases.aramaic: הֶעֱלָה עַל הַסֶּלַע אוֹ עַל הָאֶבֶן, חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: if one offered up on a rock or on a stone, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא as a two-part statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was speaking about the time when במות were allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule about a במה leads to a result for the time when במות are forbidden: one is liable.

steps.title: Are the altar's corner, ramp, base and square shape needed on a במה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asks whether the features that are required on the main מזבח are also required on a במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asked: the corner, ramp, base and square shape, do they hold things back from being valid on a במה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. Do the features that must be on the מזבח in the בית המקדש also have to be on a private altar?
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the main מזבח, missing a corner, ramp, base or square shape makes the offering invalid. The question is whether the same holds for a במה at a time when במות were allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Ramp leading up to the altar
That they hold back, meaning they are required for the offering to be valid

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, asked:
corner, ramp, base, and square shape –
what is the law, are they required at a private altar?
phrases.notes: Literally 'do they hold back', meaning: without them, is the offering not valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether a במה needs a built altar at all to which altar features a במה needs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the corner, ramp, base and square shape are required for a במה to be valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא answers: required on the public במה, not on the private one
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a ברייתא. The קרן, כבש, ריבוע and יסוד hold back (are מעכב) a במה גדולה, but they do not hold back a במה קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to him: A ברייתא teaches that the corner, the ramp, the square shape and the base are required on a great במה. They are not required on a small במה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question from step 30 by quoting a ברייתא. The answer splits the two kinds of במה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether the main מזבח's features also apply to a במה. The ברייתא says it depends on which kind of במה. On the public במה גדולה these features are מעכב, meaning the altar is not valid without them. On a private במה קטנה they are not needed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Required: without them, the altar is not valid

steps.whatToRemember: The four features (קרן, כבש, ריבוע, יסוד) are מעכב on a במה גדולה, but not on a במה קטנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as 'a במה never needs these features.' The ברייתא divides them: the public במה גדולה does need them. Only the private במה קטנה is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to step 27. There רבי שמעון learned that a במה needs no built altar at all. The ברייתא fits that idea for the private במה, but it keeps the public one closer to the rules of the main מזבח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him: It is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who asked the question in step 30.

phrases.english: The corner, the ramp, the square shape, and the base
are indispensable on a great במה,
phrases.notes: The great במה is the public altar. The small במה below is a private one.

phrases.english: but they are not indispensable on a small במה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the שאלה of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא in step 30 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The main מזבח's features (קרן, כבש, ריבוע, יסוד) are required on a במה גדולה but not on a במה קטנה.
